kind: prospectively specified project-generated study; no bank observations
question: Can a well-estimated constant residual projection mislead a population offer decision when effect heterogeneity is omitted?
assumptions: Observed binary stratum with probability one half
Assignment independent of potential-outcome noise given stratum
Potential outcomes Y(a)=50S+100Sa+epsilon in illustrative USD
Independent Gaussian noise with standard deviation 50
Offer cost 40 illustrative USD per customer
methods: Constant residual OLS with oracle nuisance functions and heteroskedastic sandwich standard error
Stratum-specific differences in means standardized to known population shares; independent-cell variance estimate
targets: Net value of universal offer at cost 40
metrics: Bias and RMSE relative to population ATE
95 percent Wald coverage for own estimand and ATE
Frequency of rejecting a positive-value universal offer
failure_rule: Stratified route unavailable if any treatment-by-stratum cell has fewer than two observations; retain failures in unconditional metrics and report conditional metrics separately.
limits: Oracle nuisance functions favour the residual comparator and isolate effect-model restriction
Gaussian constructed example does not establish real-bank returns or general coverage
No tuning or choice of scenarios after seeing outcomes
resource_limit: Six scenarios, five hundred replications each; CPU-only, at most two minutes
additional_exact_examples: Equivalent Gaussian graph models and intervention values
Four panel aggregation targets from the inherited constructed panel
Loss from a noisy confounder proxy using an exact Gaussian covariance calculation
review: The methods share the same simulated observations. Different estimands are explicitly retained. Failures remain counted. No package defect or universal superiority will be inferred. Monetary costs and noise are illustrative assumptions, not observed inputs.
